rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived "Recognized-Intangible Earnings Insolvency" (identical second leg, first leg merely nets goodwill out of intan), so it is very likely to reproduce that result with slightly noisier exposure rather than test a new mechanism.

The structure is the archived "Leveraged Goodwill Cash Failure" with oancf/lt swapped for the archived R&D-adjusted gross-surplus/lt term — a mechanical ingredient substitution combining two existing archive components, and since gross surplus is highly correlated with cash coverage the result is largely predictable.

The proposal is internally consistent (MIN of high-volatility and high-cash-surplus ranks scaled by R&D intensity does load positively where the hypothesis claims) and is motivated by a genuine diagnosed sign reversal in the archive, though the optionality story is partly post-hoc and the parent signal's fmb_tstat was near zero, so cross-sectional support may remain weak.

Identical construction to the archived "Earnings-Validated R&D Leverage Relief" with the validation leg swapped to the archive's already-known strongest driver (oancf−dlc), so any improvement will most plausibly reflect the cash-surplus effect rather than the leverage-relief idea being tested.

The mechanism — weak income coexisting with strong operating cash flow predicting higher returns — is essentially the accruals/earnings-quality anomaly (Sloan) applied to an intangible-heavy loss subsample, and it also overlaps directionally with the archived "Recognized-Intangible Cash Insolvency," limiting incremental information despite a coherently articulated amortization story.

The fmb-versus-alpha diagnosis is sensible and the expression matches the hypothesis, but applying the archive's already-used two-period MIN template to the archive's already-tested adjusted-gross-surplus term is a mechanical persistence tweak rather than a substantively different construction.
